subject: ACME billing anomaly: per-route cost slice & triage
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Liu <jared@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME billing anomaly: per-route cost slice & triage

Team — Jared from Acme looped me in: they saw an unexpected billing jump last night that appears correlated with increased calls hitting the /v1/generate route from their tenant. They asked for a quick breakdown by route and token-path to reconcile charges.

Quick summary:
- Customer: Acme Cloud (production tenant)
- Symptom: 3x token spend vs baseline for 2028-11-01 22:00–02:00 PST
- Tentative root cause: increased long-sequence calls + repeated retries hitting higher-quantized model variant

Asks:
1) Can Observability produce a per-route and per-model token-cost slice for the window (CSV) and surface any high-tail sequences?
2) Can Product weigh whether a short-term guardrail (route token cap or fallback to smaller model after N tokens) is feasible this sprint?
3) Ops: we need a playbook entry for customer billing spike investigations so we can respond faster — include what telemetry to collect.

I've attached the billing snapshot Jared sent (acme-billing-spike-snapshot.csv) and a small token-path extract (token-paths-trace.txt) he gave us.

Jared — thanks for flagging. Any additional context (recent rollout, A/B test, or client-side batching change) would help.

Rishi
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme-billing-spike-snapshot.csv (CSV, 98 KB)
Attachment: token-paths-trace.txt (TXT, 12 KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME billing anomaly: per-route cost slice & triage

Thanks Rishi — looping Observability and Runtime owners. Initial notes:
- I can produce per-route token-level breakdowns for the requested window; will need 30–45m to run the export and validate sampling bias.
- We currently have route-level counters but not a consolidated per-token-cost CSV by model variant — that's doable with the trace join we discussed in OBS-1298.

Action plan (my proposed):
- Irene to run export and post CSV to shared Drive link (ETA: today EOD).
- Naomi to run quick correlation between rollout flags and tenant timestamps (ETA: 2 hours).
- Marissa to weigh in on product guardrail options; if we want a short-term policy we need an API change or console flag.

One clarification: are we confident the spike is purely server-side (retries/batching) vs. client replays? Jared's token dump shows repeated identical prompts in short succession.

Irene
Staff Engineer, Observability

Attachment: (will add export link when ready)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME billing anomaly: per-route cost slice & triage

Putting product perspective: short-term mitigations vs. longer-term instrumentation.

Short-term (this sprint):
- Console: temporary 'route token cap' toggle per tenant — implement as a soft cap with alerting and a configurable fallback model. Low-risk server-side guardrail that can be enabled for specific tenants.
- Billing transparency: add a per-route token-cost CSV export in the Console 'billing' tab (quick UI + backend job). Implementation estimate: 3 dev days + 1 day QA.

Long-term:
- Add per-token path attribution tied to model variant and quantization profile in the runtime. This is larger (OBS-1298) but would eliminate these manual investigations.

Irene/Naomi: if the export and correlation are quick, we can decide whether to ship the short-term console cap this sprint. If not, prioritize the CSV export first so CS can reconcile with ACME and issue a credit if necessary.

Marissa
Director, Product Management

P.S. tagging JIRA: OBS-1298 for the instrumentation epic; if we go route-cap, create a small subtask under that epic with label "billing-guardrail".

From: Jared Liu <jared@acmecloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-03T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME billing anomaly: per-route cost slice & triage

Thanks Rishi/Irene/Marissa — appreciate the quick response. A few clarifications from our side:
- We did push a client change on 2028-11-01 21:50 PST that enabled a debug-mode retry loop for a subset of users (internal change, not intended for production).
- The increase shows up exclusively for our production tenant id: acme-prod-42.
- We attached the raw request IDs and timestamps in the CSV you already have; happy to share more if you need it.

If the short-term guardrail is easy to flip, please enable it for acme-prod-42 while we revert the client change. Otherwise a manual credit for the excess tokens would be appreciated — we'll coordinate with billing.

— Jared
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Cloud
